Every instance created without an explicit queued value will therefore carry the same import-time timestamp rather than the time of the assignment. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. This makes the queued field misleading now and will break any future logic that relies on it for age checks, metrics, debouncing, or auditing."

Celery task payloads should be serializable and round-trippable, but a raw datetime may fail JSON serialization, and if a custom encoder converts it to a string, `AssignmentSource.from_dict` does not parse it back into a datetime. This can cause task-publishing failures or rehydrate an object whose `queued` field no longer matches its declared type. Serialize `queued` explicitly, for example as an ISO-8601 string with corresponding parsing in `from_dict`, or omit it from the task payload if it is not needed."

If a Sentry group is linked to multiple external issues in the same integration, an inbound assignment change from one issue will not be propagated to the others, leaving their assignees out of sync. Consider carrying and comparing the originating external issue identifier, or explicitly document that same-integration suppression is intentionally integration-wide."

If a non-empty assignment source dictionary is malformed, missing required fields, or contains unexpected fields due to serialization or version skew, the same-integration cycle protection is silently lost and the outbound sync may propagate back to the originating integration. At minimum, log or emit a metric when a provided assignment source cannot be parsed; alternatively make parsing tolerant of unknown fields while still validating required ones."

findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The dataclass default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` when the class is imported, not when an AssignmentSource is created. Every instance created without an explicit queued value will therefore carry the same import-time timestamp rather than the time of the assignment. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. This makes the queued field misleading now and will break any future logic that relies on it for age checks, metrics, debouncing, or auditing.

findings.title: AssignmentSource payload sent to Celery is not safely round-trippable
findings.body: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` places `assignment_source.to_dict()` directly into Celery task kwargs. `to_dict()` returns the `queued` field as a raw `datetime` object. Celery task payloads should be serializable and round-trippable, but a raw datetime may fail JSON serialization, and if a custom encoder converts it to a string, `AssignmentSource.from_dict` does not parse it back into a datetime. This can cause task-publishing failures or rehydrate an object whose `queued` field no longer matches its declared type. Serialize `queued` explicitly, for example as an ISO-8601 string with corresponding parsing in `from_dict`, or omit it from the task payload if it is not needed.

findings.title: Cycle suppression is integration-wide rather than scoped to the originating external issue
findings.body: `should_sync` suppresses outbound syncing whenever the assignment source integration matches the target installation integration. Because `AssignmentSource` only carries an integration ID and not the originating external issue, every linked external issue for that integration is skipped. If a Sentry group is linked to multiple external issues in the same integration, an inbound assignment change from one issue will not be propagated to the others, leaving their assignees out of sync. Consider carrying and comparing the originating external issue identifier, or explicitly document that same-integration suppression is intentionally integration-wide.

findings.title: Invalid assignment source dict silently disables cycle protection
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns `None` when parsing fails, and `sync_assignee_outbound` then proceeds as if no assignment source existed. If a non-empty assignment source dictionary is malformed, missing required fields, or contains unexpected fields due to serialization or version skew, the same-integration cycle protection is silently lost and the outbound sync may propagate back to the originating integration. At minimum, log or emit a metric when a provided assignment source cannot be parsed; alternatively make parsing tolerant of unknown fields while still validating required ones.

findings.title: Missing suppression test for deassign with a matching assignment source
findings.body: The PR adds a test showing that `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with a matching `AssignmentSource` suppresses outbound sync, but there is no equivalent test for `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign`. Since `deassign` was also changed to accept and forward `assignment_source`, add a test that deassigns with `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` and asserts that `sync_assignee_outbound` is not called for the same integration.
